source_text: Quis nollet curam nos agere animae de uictu et corpori de uestitu, nisi qui ista homini ante prospexit et exinde praestans merito curam eorum tamquam aemulam liberalitatis suae prohibet, qui et substantiam ipsius animae accommodauit potiorem esca et materiam ipsius corporis figurauit potiorem tunica, cuius et corui non serunt nec metunt nec in apothecas condunt et tamen aluntur ab ipso, cuius et lilia et foenum non texunt nec neunt et tamen uestiuntur ab ipso, cuius et Salomon gloriosissimus nec ullo tamen flosculo cultior?
pass_a_gloss: Who would not want us to take care of the soul with regard to food and the body with regard to clothing, except He who foresaw these things for man beforehand and, providing them from that point on, deservedly prohibits the care of them as if it were a rival of His own generosity, who also prepared the substance of the soul itself with food more abundantly and shaped the material of the body itself with clothing more abundantly, whose ravens neither sow nor reap nor store in barns and yet are fed by Him, whose lilies and grasses neither spin nor sew and yet are clothed by Him, whose Solomon, most glorious, was not more cultivated with any flower?

choices.why: aemulam is used to describe something that rivals or competes with something else
ab ipso is used to indicate the agent performing the action

bible_refs.note: corui non serunt nec metunt nec in apothecas condunt
lilia non texunt nec neunt et tamen uestiuntur
Salomon gloriosissimus nec ullo tamen flosculo cultior

pass_b_english: Who would not want us to take care of the soul regarding food and the body regarding clothing, except the One who foresaw these needs for humanity in advance and, by supplying them, rightly forbids anxiety over them as a rival to his own generosity? He even furnished the soul's very substance with food more abundantly and fashioned the body's very material with clothing more abundantly. His ravens neither sow nor reap nor store in barns, yet he feeds them (Luke 12:24). His lilies and grasses neither spin nor sew, yet they are clothed by him (Matthew 6:28-29). Even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like a single one of these flowers (Matthew 6:29).

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful continuous translation, while Pass B provides a more readable version with necessary scripture citations (Luke 12:24, Matthew 6:28-29, Matthew 6:29) which are correctly identified in the notes. The comparison of the soul to food and the body to clothing is preserved. The nuances of 'aemulam' (rival) and 'ab ipso' (by Him) are correctly handled.
